Dylan / all — quick technical readout after reviewing the spreadsheet and routing patterns. TL;DR: we can meet tighter RTOs for a scoped subset of routes if Banklytics accepts a constrained operational model. Details: 

1) Activation path: we can provide warm-standby pools in us-east that maintain loaded KV caches for the declared critical routing group. That requires a persistent reserved capacity (per-region VMs/GPUs) and a short pre-warm handshake (30–60s) to attach live KV shards. A true 30m RTO is achievable; the biggest risk is traffic rehydration for non-cached prefixes.

2) RPO 5m: Achievable only if Banklytics adopts our incremental replication stream (near-real-time) for the critical dataset and allows a modest write-fallback window. If they insist on synchronous cross-region writes, cost and latency increase significantly.

3) Operational controls we need from Banklytics:
- A clearly defined critical routing group list (names + routes) to scope caching requirements.
- A scheduled heartbeat/replication test window during onboarding so we can validate failover in advance.

4) Risks: post-failover cold caches for non-critical traffic, transient latency spikes during routing convergence, and increased token consumption during rehydration.

I can draft the one-paragraph exception with the operational checklist. Will also include rollback criteria and measurable test steps.

Hannah Schmitt

Folks — couple of legal/product guardrails and a proposed template for an exception. High level: I support offering a time-boxed operational carveout with clear caps and a credit schedule. Proposed terms (draft language below) — I’ll attach a PDF with redlines.

Proposed temporary exception (summary):
- Scope: Applies only to the "critical routing group" defined in Annex A (to be signed); does not change Redwood’s general SLA.
- Activation: Redwood will maintain reserved warm-standby capacity in the nominated region(s) and will use near-real-time replication for the scoped dataset.
- RTO / RPO: Target RTO 30 minutes; target RPO 5 minutes for Annex A scope. These are operational targets, not service credits triggers, unless Redwood fails to meet them in two consecutive validated failovers.
- Duration: 90-day pilot beginning on the activation date; renewable by mutual written agreement.
- Capacity Caps & Credits: If Redwood cannot meet the target RTO/RPO during a declared DR incident affecting Annex A, Banklytics will be entitled to a service credit equal to 6% of the monthly invoice for each missed RTO occurrence, capped at 30% for the month.
- Termination & Liability: No expansion of indemnity; Redwood’s liability remains subject to the baseline agreement.

Notes: we should avoid language that makes the RTO/RPO automatic credit triggers on single transient events. Instead require validation: the customer must declare an incident, we run a post-incident runbook and independent validation; only verified misses count toward credits.

Marissa — please run a pricing uplift for the 90-day pilot (warm-standby reserved capacity + support runway). I’ll produce a one-page amendment and send as PDF for review.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Policy | Redwood Inference
